newsitem.title: JAPAN: New Japan firm to set up for unlisted stock trade.
newsitem.headline: New Japan firm to set up for unlisted stock trade.

text.p: A brokerage house specialising in trading unlisted shares is due to be established next week as the first Japanese brokerage to be formed after the nation lifted a ban on brokerages on trading of such shares on Tuesday as a part of the "Big Bang" financial deregulation.

D-Brain Securities Co Ltd is likely to get a brokerage license from the Ministry of Finance by the end of this month, said an official of Japanese consulting firm D-Brain Co Ltd, which is due to set up the brokerage next Monday.
The official said that the ministry had informally told the firm that it would grant the license.

The securities house, to be headed by an official from the "Big Four" brokerage Daiwa Securities Co Ltd, will be capitalised at 180 million yen, he said, without disclosing the president's name. D-Brain Co will contribute 28.3 percent of the capital, he added.
"The new firm would trade unlisted shares for both individual and institutional investors," the official said. The brokerage will start full operation from late August, he added.
The move followed the late June announcement by regional Japanese brokerage Ark Securities Co Ltd that it would start broking unlisted shares in firms set up by venture capitals.
Ark Securities, based in Aichi prefecture of central Japan, said it would start the broking operation on July 1 for individual investors. -- Tokyo Equities Desk, +81-3-3432-9404
